text:
toni: Morning all, first-day snag. Okta prompts me to register a passkey but registration fails with "Could not reach authenticator". I'm on Ubuntu 22.04 laptop using a YubiKey 5 NFC (NFC + USB-C). Also 1Password web shows "account org mismatch" when I try to sign in with my corporate email (toni@redwood.com) even though I accepted an invite earlier. Finally, ssh-agent forwarding seems broken to the jump host (Agent admitted failure to sign using the key). Who do I loop in?

sam: Welcome, and congrats! :tada: For the passkey error, try `navigator.credentials` tests in browser console or register via mobile Okta app using NFC. On Linux you might also need pcscd running for NFC. Can you run `systemctl status pcscd` and `lsusb`?

toni: pcscd is inactive. lsusb shows `Bus 002 Device 010: ID 1050:0127 Yubico.com YubiKey 5`. I started pcscd but still failing. Browser console shows `NotAllowedError: The request is not allowed by the user agent or the platform in the current context.`

people-ops: Re: 1Password, did you accept the invite to toni@redwood.com or to a personal alias? If you accepted with a personal email that can cause organization conflict. We can transfer the seat, pinging PEOPLE-5032.

toni: I accepted the invite sent to toni.work+dev@gmail (I was trying to avoid typos). Oops. Please resend to corporate.

devops: For SSH agent: paste output of `ssh -vvv -A dev-jump` (sanitized). Common culprits: gpg-agent vs ssh-agent conflicts, or keys not loaded into agent. On Ubuntu, `gpg-agent` can be the SSH agent. Run `ssh-add -l` and `gpg --card-status` if you're using a smartcard-backed key.

toni: `ssh-add -l` returns "The agent has no identities". I thought my key was loaded. I use gpg for commit signing but not for SSH. `gpg --card-status` returns "No card available".

sam: OK two things: 1) start ssh-agent: `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"` then `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. 2) For NFC YubiKey on Linux, ensure `ykman` can talk to the device: `ykman info` and `ykman fido info`. If pcscd was inactive it explains NFC failures. Restart it and test again.

toni: Ran `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"` and `ssh-add` succeeded. SSH to jump now works. Thanks.

it-help: Opening ticket IT-2701 to help with YubiKey/NFC and 1Password seat transfer. If you want quick passkey enrollment, use Okta mobile (NFC) or plug the key directly and use USB flow. Also check chrome://flags for WebAuthn on Linux.

security-bot: Policy check: New devices must have disk encryption and screen lock enabled before full org access is granted. Please confirm FileVault/UEFI disk encryption equivalent enabled on your laptop.

toni: Laptop disk encrypted (LUKS) and screen lock enabled.

people-ops: PEOPLE-5032 created and seat transfer requested. New invite sent to toni@redwood.com. Reply when accepted.

sam: Quick note: after pcscd restart I saw `ykman fido info` working on my test box. If `ykman` still errors for you, try `sudo usermod -aG plugdev $USER` then log out/in. Also add udev rules from Yubico docs if needed.

toni: Accepted the corporate 1Password invite. Tried `ykman fido info` and now it returns device info. Okta passkey enrollment succeeded via USB flow. All green now. Thanks for the fast help :raised_hands:

it-help: IT-2701 status = Resolved (notes: started pcscd, added user to plugdev, restarted ykman, reissued 1Password invite). If anything else pops up, reopen the ticket.

toni: All set. Appreciate everyone's help!"
